scope: Papers authored or co-authored by F. Ghezelbash found in SpineBench donwload/ and plan_agent/validation papers/ (read-only). Card snapshot read on the same date.

status_legend.covered: all experimental data of the comparison are booked as tasks
status_legend.partly: some of the data are booked

type_legend.model_vs_experiment: paper's own model vs measured data
type_legend.literature_compilation: review table of published measurements (no own model)

papers.title: Subject-specific biomechanics of trunk: musculoskeletal scaling, internal loads and intradiscal pressure estimation
papers.model: Sagittally symmetric kinematics-driven nonlinear FE musculoskeletal trunk model (T1-S1, Abaqus), 126 muscles with wrapping, T11-S1 nonlinear beam motion segments; personalised by sex/age/BH/BW (Anderson 2012, Shi 2014); L4-L5 IDP from a new compression-rotation regression (Eq. 6).

comparisons.output: L4-L5 IDP in vivo
comparisons.conditions: 11 tasks: upright relaxed; 19.8 kg close / away; flexion 10, 30, 50 deg; full flexion 107 deg; flexion 70 deg + 19.8 kg; one-handed asymmetric lift 19.8 kg; lateral bending 10 and 20 deg (model scaled to Wilke subject)
comparisons.result: matched (largest misses: upright 0.33 vs 0.47 MPa; flex 70 deg + 19.8 kg 2.65 vs 2.3 MPa)
comparisons.note: Not booked: one-handed asymmetric lift (~1.0 MPa) and lateral bending 10 deg (~0.48 MPa). Both in Wilke 2001 (P02_Wilke2001.pdf, catalogued) and readable from Fig 5.

comparisons.output: Back muscle activity vs trunk flexion angle (LGPT, ICPT, L/R), flexion-relaxation
comparisons.conditions: Unloaded forward flexion 0-107 deg, single male subject (52 y, 68.4 kg, 174.5 cm)
comparisons.result: matched (pattern and FR onset ~60-80 deg; model LGPT peak 22% vs EMG ~20%)
comparisons.note: Arjmand 2010 J Biomech 43:485 (not in donwload); same subject/protocol in Arjmand 2009 Clin Biomech (donwload/Arjmand2009CB.pdf, catalogued as msk_idp_lumbar). Curve digitisable from Fig 6a.

comparisons.output: Muscle activity in MVE extension (242 Nm) and flexion (151 Nm): LGPT, ICPT, MF, RA, EO, IO
comparisons.conditions: Semi-seated MVE, mean of 12 males; IAP 0/10/25 kPa and antagonist moment variants I-V
comparisons.result: matched (extension); moderate in flexion (RA/EO under-predicted without IAP)

comparisons.output: Muscle activity in axial-torque MVE (78.3 Nm + coupled lateral/flexion), ICPT, MF, RA, EO, IO, both sides
comparisons.conditions: Upright standing, right axial torque; model scaled to 30 y, 73 kg, 179.9 cm
comparisons.result: mostly matched (left EO/IO, right IO); right RA/EO and right ICPT under-predicted
comparisons.note: Left-side muscles under right torque = mirror of the right-side tasks under left torque (emg_st_axl_ng_*).

model_vs_model.output: L4-L5 IDP vs compression and flexion rotation
model_vs_model.compared_with: Detailed lumbar FE model (Shirazi-Adl 2006), Dreischarf 2013 relation (IDP = P/0.77), Shirazi-Adl & Drouin 1988 (L2-L3)
model_vs_model.result: differences grow with compression and rotation; earlier relations ignore rotation

model_vs_model.output: L4-L5 compression and shear in forward flexion
model_vs_model.compared_with: 4 personal-parameter sets (subjects of Wilke, Arjmand, El Ouaaid, Ng)

papers.title: Trunk musculoskeletal response in maximum voluntary exertions: a combined measurement-modeling investigation
papers.model: Same subject-specific KD nonlinear FE musculoskeletal trunk model (126 muscles), semi-seated posture with reduced lordosis, driven by each subject's measured MVE moments; 19 subjects (9 F, 10 M).

comparisons.output: Muscle activity in flexion and extension MVE (LGPT, ICPT T-level and L3, MF, RA, EO, IO; both sides)
comparisons.result: matched (qualitatively good; MF over-predicted in extension)
comparisons.note: Card books L/R mean and IC at L3; the thoracic-level ICPT electrode is not booked.

comparisons.output: Muscle activity in right/left lateral MVE
comparisons.conditions: Own data, 4 subjects with least coupled moments simulated
comparisons.result: not matched (weak; ipsilateral EO/IO and MF under-predicted)
comparisons.note: Only right-side electrodes booked; left-side bars of Fig 5 not booked (owner data).

comparisons.output: Muscle activity in right/left axial MVE
comparisons.note: Only right-side electrodes booked; left-side bars of Fig 6 not booked (owner data).

comparisons.output: Measured MVE primary and coupled moments (F, M) vs literature
comparisons.result: own moments in range; women exerted more than other female cohorts
comparisons.note: Experiment-vs-literature (no model). Not booked: Azghani 2009, Cholewicki 1995, Kumar 1996, Lee & Kuo 2000, Malchaire 1995, McNeill 1980, Parnianpour 1988a/b, Plamondon 2014, Keller 2002.

comparisons.output: Estimated peak muscle stress needed to reach MVE (sigma_max)
comparisons.metric: within range (0.80 +/- 0.42 MPa; <1.5 MPa in 95% of muscles)
comparisons.note: No SpineBench card for muscle stress. Burkhart (J Biomech 2018) is catalogued (msk_mvc_coupled); Buchanan 1995 (elbow) and Pruim 1980 (jaw) are not spine data.

papers.title: On the modeling of human intervertebral disc annulus fibrosus: elastic, permanent deformation and failure responses
papers.model: Non-homogeneous fibre-reinforced AF model: Mooney-Rivlin-type matrix plus collagen fibres (types I/II) with elastic, plastic (permanent deformation) and damage/failure laws (Abaqus); applied to tissue specimens and an L2-L3 disc-body-unit model.

comparisons.output: AF stress-strain, uniaxial along fibres (single lamella)
comparisons.note: Skaggs 1994 (fibre-direction curves) not in SpineBench; not downloaded.

comparisons.output: AF stress-strain, uniaxial circumferential (multilayer)
comparisons.note: Acaroglu 1995 and Skrzypiec 2007 curves not booked (not downloaded).

comparisons.output: AF axial (toe-region) modulus, uniaxial axial
comparisons.note: Card books the curves; modulus is derivable.

comparisons.output: AF equi-biaxial circumferential stress-strain
comparisons.note: Card books the circ-fixed O'Connell 2012 curve (via Ghezelbash 2021), not the equi-biaxial curve used here.

comparisons.output: AF failure stress and failure strain, circumferential
comparisons.note: Card notes exclude failure data. Not downloaded.

comparisons.output: AF failure stress vs modulus, fibre direction
comparisons.note: Not downloaded.

comparisons.output: AF axial failure stress (bone-AF-bone)
comparisons.note: Green1993.pdf is in donwload/ and catalogued (passive_tissue, usable=yes) but excluded by the card.

comparisons.output: Disc-body-unit axial compression force-displacement (L2-L3)
comparisons.conditions: Compression to 4500 N, with/without 350 N preconditioning, Poisson ratio variants
comparisons.note: Card books only linear axial stiffness values (Tencer 1982, Costi 2008, Amin 2016, Berkson 1979, Frei 2002), not the force-displacement curves. Jamison2013.pdf, Marini2016.pdf, Tencer1982 are in donwload/ (catalogued); Asano 1992, Brown 1957, Markolf & Morris 1974 not downloaded. Curves also digitisable from Ghezelbash 2020a Fig 4a.

comparisons.output: Cyclic compression-tension of an intact motion segment
comparisons.note: Asano 1992 not downloaded.

comparisons.output: Cyclic compression-tension of a disc-body unit
comparisons.note: Marini2016.pdf catalogued (fe_model_comparison, usable=no) but not booked.

comparisons.output: AF residual-stress opening angle after radial transection
comparisons.result: not matched (11 deg vs 28 and 53 deg); attributed to swelling not modelled
comparisons.note: Bovine data; probably out of scope for SpineBench.

model_vs_model.compared_with: Schmidt 2007 hyperelastic AF model (and Peng 2006, Shahraki 2015 cited)
model_vs_model.result: proposed model closer to tissue tests

model_vs_model.compared_with: Own model with Poisson ratio 0.499 vs 0.49999 and plasticity parameter variants

papers.title: Internal load-sharing in the human passive lumbar spine: review of in vitro and finite element model studies
papers.model: Review (no own model); compiles in vitro measurements and FE predictions of load-sharing among disc, ligaments and facets.

comparisons.output: Facet joint forces in vitro (compiled table)
comparisons.conditions: Moments 7.5-15 Nm, compression/shear preloads, L1-S1 levels
comparisons.note: Wilson 2006 (L3-L4, 7.5 Nm extension/axial, min/max) not booked; catalogued.

comparisons.output: Load-sharing fractions disc/ligaments/facets
comparisons.conditions: Flexion (fresh and after creep), anterior/posterior shear up to 250 N; resection-based
comparisons.note: No load-sharing card. In vitro rows (Adams 1980/1987, Lu 2005) not downloaded; FE rows are model-vs-model (below).

comparisons.output: Stepwise resection effects on ROM / IDP
comparisons.conditions: Force-controlled pure moments with sequential resection
comparisons.note: Heuer 2007b IDP-with-resection rows are in idp_invitro (l45s_*).

model_vs_model.compared_with: FE studies: Naserkhaki 2016, Schmidt 2013a, Sharma 1995, Shirazi-Adl & Drouin 1987 vs in vitro Adams 1980/1987, Lu 2005
model_vs_model.result: FE and in vitro broadly consistent; protocol (resection order, BCs, preload) drives differences

papers.title: Subject-specific regression equations to estimate lower spinal loads during symmetric and asymmetric static lifting
papers.file: donwload/Mitutoyo Digital Caliper - Certificate of Calibration Control # DDE14R52L.PDF (mis-named IRSST accepted manuscript); also plan_agent/validation papers/1-s2.0-S0021929019308073-main.pdf
papers.model: Subject-specific KD nonlinear FE musculoskeletal trunk model driven by measured T11/S1 rotations of 19 subjects (64 lifting tasks, 3840 simulations) -> regression equations for L4-L5/L5-S1 compression and shear; IDP via 2016 Eq. 6.

comparisons.output: L4-L5 IDP in vivo (regression equations)
comparisons.conditions: Takahashi: upright, +10 kg, flexion 10/20/30 deg with/without 10 kg; Wilke: stand, 20 kg close/away, flexion 10/30/50, full, 70 deg + 19.8 kg; Sato: 8 subjects individually, upright and flexed
comparisons.note: Sato 1999 compared per subject (16 values); card books the cohort mean only. Individual values in Sato 1999 Table 2.

comparisons.output: L4-L5 IDP vs axial rotation angle (-17 to +25 deg)
comparisons.result: partly matched (under-predicted near neutral, ~0.27 vs ~0.45 MPa; matched at large angles)
comparisons.note: Card books only the maximal-twist point (24 deg). Wilke 2001 IDP-vs-angle curve (P02_Wilke2001.pdf) could be added as several angle tasks.

comparisons.output: L4-L5 IDP vs lateral bending angle (-30 to +30 deg), FE-MS model driven by Narimani & Arjmand 2018 kinematics
comparisons.result: partly matched (within band at small/moderate angles; over-predicted at 30 deg)
comparisons.note: Card books only 20 deg. Wilke 2001 curve could be added.

comparisons.output: Back muscle EMG (LGPT T11, ICPT T11 and L3, MF L4; L/R) in static holds
comparisons.conditions: Own data: 19 subjects, 14 kg at 4 heights (mid-tibia, knee, mid-femur, upright) x 4 asymmetry angles (0-90 deg)
comparisons.result: moderate (good in symmetric tasks, weak in asymmetric)
comparisons.note: Booked: symmetric 4 heights (L/R mean) and asymmetry 0-90 deg at mid-femur for LG(T11)/MF(L4). Not booked: other height x asymmetry cells, IC asymmetric tasks.

comparisons.output: Abdominal EMG (RA, EO, IO; L/R) in static holds
comparisons.note: Owner data; readable from Fig 6.

model_vs_model.compared_with: Regression equations vs the FE-MS model they were fitted to
Other lifting tools (Arjmand 2011/2012 regressions, AnyBody; via Rajaee 2015)

papers.title: Modeling of human intervertebral disc annulus fibrosus with complex multi-fiber networks
papers.model: Micromechanical layerwise AF model (lamellae, inter-lamellar matrix, elastic fibres, cross-links) and microplane / hyperelastic AF models; single-equivalent-layer vs layerwise approaches; L2-L3 whole-disc model.

comparisons.output: AF stress-strain along fibres
comparisons.note: Skaggs 1994 not booked.

comparisons.output: AF circumferential uniaxial, geometry-matched specimens
comparisons.conditions: Rectangular (7.73 x 2.87 x 1.35 mm) and necked (Skrzypiec) specimens
comparisons.note: Skrzypiec 2007 not booked.

comparisons.output: AF circumferential uniaxial, cross specimen
AF biaxial (circ-fixed) circumferential and axial stress
comparisons.conditions: Axial stretch with circumferential strain held at 0; 0.5 N preload; sample-geometry variants
comparisons.note: Wagner & Lotz is booked as the mean-coefficient fit, not their biaxial run.

comparisons.output: AF biaxial (circ-fixed) axial stress, square specimen
Effect of specimen geometry on circumferential response
comparisons.note: Compiled scatter; low priority.

comparisons.output: Whole-disc axial compression force-displacement (L2-L3)
comparisons.conditions: Disc height 11 mm, area 1695 mm2; several AF laws
comparisons.result: matched (all AF laws inside the band)
comparisons.note: Card books only linear axial stiffness values (Tencer 1982, Costi 2008, Amin 2016, Berkson 1979, Frei 2002), not the force-displacement curves. Jamison2013.pdf, Marini2016.pdf, Tencer1982 are in donwload/ (catalogued); Asano 1992, Brown 1957, Markolf & Morris 1974 not downloaded. Curves also digitisable from Ghezelbash 2020a Fig 4a.

model_vs_model.compared_with: Published hyperelastic SEFs: Peng 2006, Ayturk 2012, Marini 2016, Stadelmann 2018, Momeni-Shahraki 2015, Yang & O'Connell, Jacobs 2013 (Table 1)
model_vs_model.result: all match whole-disc compression; some too stiff/compliant in uniaxial/biaxial tissue tests
different local fields, similar gross response

papers.title: Submaximal electromyography-driven musculoskeletal modeling of the human trunk during static tasks: equilibrium and stability analyses
papers.model: Subject-specific EMG-assisted-optimisation multi-joint trunk model (KD-FE based) with stability analysis; gains calibrated from maximal or submaximal ramp MVC data; 30 subjects (15 F, 15 M; Lariviere 2019 cohort).

comparisons.output: Muscle moments from calibrated EMG-driven model vs measured (required) moments, T11-T12 to L5-S1
comparisons.conditions: Ramp MVCs in 6 directions, semi-seated; maximal vs submaximal calibration, with/without axial tasks
comparisons.metric: Pearson r 0.75-0.77 (relative error 41-44%); 0.91-0.92 (28%) without axial torque
comparisons.result: moderate; good when axial tasks excluded
comparisons.note: This cohort's MVC moments are not in maximal_exertions (Lariviere 2019 is booked only in emg_load_holding, lar19_*). Per-subject moments are not tabulated in the paper; would need the IRSST dataset.

model_vs_model.output: L5-S1 compression, stability index, sum of abdominal / long back muscle forces
model_vs_model.compared_with: Maximal vs submaximal calibration (9 standing hold tasks)

papers.title: Effect of personalized spinal profile on its biomechanical response in an EMG-assisted optimization musculoskeletal model of the trunk
papers.model: Subject-specific multi-joint EMG-kinematics-assisted optimisation trunk model (Eskandari 2023) with generic vs personalised (skin-profile) spine curvature; 31 participants (healthy and chronic LBP).

comparisons.output: Pattern of predicted muscle forces (IC, LG, MF, RA, EO, IO) vs surface EMG across conditions
comparisons.conditions: Upright static holds: load height P1-P3 and distance P2 vs P4, 0 vs 6-7 kg
comparisons.result: Distance study: back muscles and IO matched, RA/EO diverged; Height study: generally not matched
comparisons.note: Analogous healthy-cohort protocol booked from Lariviere 2019 (lar19_*); the 2024 cohort EMG is non-normalised and not booked (catalogued, usable=partly).

model_vs_model.output: 17 outcomes (muscle forces, ratios, spinal loads, stability)
model_vs_model.result: medium/large effects on muscle forces; negligible/small on loads and stability

papers.title: Development and validation of a subject-specific integrated finite element musculoskeletal model of human trunk with ergonomic and clinical applications
papers.model: Subject-specific coupled FE-MS trunk model: detailed T12-S1 FE ligamentous spine (AF model of 2021, facets, ligaments) integrated with the musculature; parametric scaling (Tang 2019/2022 SSM, Anderson 2012); kinematics-driven; applications to exoskeleton, nucleotomy and fusion.

comparisons.output: AF biaxial (circ-fixed) circumferential and axial stress
comparisons.conditions: Outer AF, circumferential strain held at 0
comparisons.result: matched (model at upper edge of the +/-SD band)
comparisons.note: Bass 2004 +/-SD band and Hollingsworth & Wagner 2011 not booked.

comparisons.output: Flexion moment-rotation (ROM) curves, L1-L5 and L1-L2 ... L5-S1
comparisons.conditions: 0-5 Nm (segments) and 0-10 Nm (L1-L5); model BH 160-190 cm, BMI 19-30, both sexes
comparisons.note: Card books single moment levels; Guan 2007 only at L4-L5. Guan 2007 other levels and low-moment Panjabi points could be added (Guan 2007 catalogued).

comparisons.output: Disc-body-unit compression force-displacement (L2-L3)
comparisons.note: Card books only linear axial stiffness values (Tencer 1982, Costi 2008, Amin 2016, Berkson 1979, Frei 2002), not the force-displacement curves. Jamison2013.pdf, Marini2016.pdf, Tencer1982 are in donwload/ (catalogued); Asano 1992, Brown 1957, Markolf & Morris 1974 not downloaded. Curves also digitisable from Ghezelbash 2020a Fig 4a.

comparisons.output: L2-L3 IDP vs axial compression in vitro
comparisons.note: Brinckmann & Grootenboer 1991 (Spine 16:641) not catalogued; 3 points with SD readable from Fig 2d.

comparisons.output: L4-L5 IDP in vivo
comparisons.note: Sato 1999 per-subject values not booked.

comparisons.output: LGPT/ICPT activity (L/R) vs flexion angle, no load, single subject
comparisons.conditions: Forward flexion 0-100 deg; 169 cm, 67 kg, 27 y
comparisons.note: Booked at 25/50/95 deg only.

comparisons.output: LG/IC activity vs flexion angle (4 load heights), 10 kg
Abdominal activity (RA, EO, IO) vs flexion angle, 10 kg
comparisons.note: Owner data; readable from Fig 3d.

model_vs_model.output: IDP, AF stress, facet contact, muscle forces
model_vs_model.compared_with: With vs without exoskeleton (Koopman 2020 / Naf 2018 kinematics); intact vs L5-S1 nucleotomy vs L4-L5 fusion (Nie 2019 kinematics)
model_vs_model.result: exo: IDP 2.2 -> 1.9 MPa; fusion: adjacent IDP 1.58 -> 1.72 MPa
